name: CULTURE & SENSITIVITY - PUS
description: Pus Culture & Sensitivity identifies bacterial pathogens in pus samples and determines antibiotic susceptibility. This test guides targeted antimicrobial therapy for skin and soft tissue infections.

testdetails.method: Conventional Culture with Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing
testdetails.instrumentation: Automated Culture Systems (BD BACTEC, bioMérieux VITEK)

literatureReview: Pus Culture & Sensitivity is essential for diagnosing and treating skin and soft tissue infections. Common pathogens include Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and anaerobes. Sample collection requires sterile technique to avoid contamination. Inoculated onto blood agar, MacConkey agar, and anaerobic media. Incubated at 35-37°C for 24-48 hours. Antibiotic susceptibility testing performed using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion or automated systems. Results guide appropriate antibiotic selection. Critical for managing abscesses, cellulitis, and surgical site infections. Mixed infections may require multiple antibiotics. TAT is typically 48-72 hours for final susceptibility results.
